stem: Why is cranial radiotherapy avoided whenever possible in children under 5 years of age?

options.text: It causes immediate and permanent alopecia
It carries a high risk of profound neurocognitive damage
It is ineffective against paediatric brain tumours
Children are too small to undergo radiotherapy
It always causes irreversible hearing loss

explanation: Profound neurocognitive damage is the main concern. The young brain is still developing, so cranial radiotherapy can cause long-term impairment in cognition, learning, and development.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because alopecia can occur with radiotherapy, but it is usually not permanent and is not the main reason for avoiding treatment in very young children.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the young brain is still developing, and cranial radiotherapy can cause long-term reductions in IQ, learning difficulties, and developmental delay.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because cranial radiotherapy can be effective against some paediatric brain tumours, but it is avoided when possible in young children because of toxicity to the developing brain.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because size is not the main limitation; the concern is the biological harm of radiation to the developing nervous system.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because hearing loss can occur in some settings, but it is not the primary reason cranial radiotherapy is avoided in children under 5 years of age.

source.hint: Think about the vulnerability of an organ that is still actively growing and forming connections.
